title: Low iron: how to get tested and treated through your AI
summary: This low iron treatment guide covers 2026 ferritin cutoffs, daily vs. alternate-day oral iron, lab orders, and a $40 FutureClinic online doctor visit.
body_markdown:
A FutureClinic doctor can order ferritin, a complete blood count (CBC), and transferrin saturation (TSAT) at discounted lab prices, read them against 2026 ferritin cutoffs of 30 or 50 ng/mL, and start daily or alternate-day oral iron if it's right for you. Seeing ferritin marked normal on a lab portal despite fatigue is common, even though a 2025[JAMA review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40159291/) reports absolute iron deficiency in 14% of US adults and iron-deficiency anemia, the most common anemia ([NHLBI](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/anemia/iron-deficiency-anemia) ), in 10 million.

Your doctor can order blood tests at discounted lab prices and help with other problems in their specialty, while every FutureClinic doctor you see, specialists included, works from[one medical record](https://futureclinic.com/blog/one-online-doctor-for-everything-vs-condition-apps) . ## Why do standard lab reports miss low iron?


Untreated iron deficiency progresses to anemia. In high-income countries, 38% of nonpregnant reproductive-age women have iron deficiency without anemia, 13% have iron-deficiency anemia, and up to 84% of third-trimester pregnant women are iron deficient ([JAMA, 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40159291/) ). While the World Health Organization (2020) used a 15 ng/mL ferritin cutoff for healthy adults, the American Society of Hematology (ASH)[2026 guidelines](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42747316/) and[snapshot](https://www.hematology.org/-/media/hematology/files/clinicians/guidelines/ash-cpg-diagnosis-of-id-snapshot.pdf) note lab ranges often include deficient values, causing underdiagnosis. Doctors order a CBC, hemoglobin, iron, transferrin saturation (TSAT), and ferritin, using ASH's 2026 ferritin cutoffs:


-


**30 ng/mL or lower:** Suggested over 15 ng/mL for nonpregnant adults, menstruating people, and pregnant patients (flagged for ages 11+).


-


**50 ng/mL or lower:** Appropriate with symptoms (fatigue, pica, restless legs), heavy periods, upcoming surgery, or pregnancy plans, and may fit pregnant patients with anemia.


-


**20 ng/mL or lower:** Suggested over 12 ng/mL for ages 9 months to 4 years.


-


**Below 100 ng/mL or TSAT below 20%:** Used with inflammation (cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, infection). Draw TSAT after a 5 to 9 hour fast without iron or multivitamins.


## AI low iron treatment: how care by message compares with an office visit


In AMN Healthcare's 2025 survey of 15 US metros, new-patient physician waits averaged 31 days (23.5 in family medicine, 40 in gastroenterology, 42 in obstetrics/gynecology), and an[AJMC study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26295356/) found office visits average 121 minutes (37 travel, 84 at the clinic). Because real care takes hours, FutureClinic replies typically come within a few hours, almost always the same day or the next.

An in-person clinic suits cases needing endoscopy or IV iron. The American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) recommends upper endoscopy and colonoscopy for men and postmenopausal women with iron-deficiency anemia, and suggests it for premenopausal women. IV iron (Injectafer, carrying an August 2026 Boxed Warning for severe low phosphate; Monoferric; Feraheme) requires vein infusion and 30-minute observation, advised by the[2024 AGA update](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38864796/) when oral iron fails, is not tolerated, or is poorly absorbed after bariatric surgery or in active inflammatory bowel disease.


## What does messaging the same doctor over months do for low iron?


Restoring iron often takes 3 to 6 months. Messaging the same doctor time after time in one chat, however long in between, lets you build trust, try treatments together, and track progress. Your physician checks causes such as blood loss (heavy periods, ulcers, colon cancer, NSAIDs), malabsorption (celiac disease, H. pylori, atrophic gastritis, bariatric surgery), diet, pregnancy, or endurance sports, and can order celiac blood tests (AGA adds noninvasive H. pylori testing after negative endoscopy). That same doctor checks your 4-week hemoglobin response ([BSG 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8515119/) ), adjusts dosing for stomach upset, and tracks repeat ferritin against baseline.

They span more than 60 specialties, and every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record.
